what I did was skim the stream IR and noticed some ops didn't have affinities. all stream ops should generally have affinities. then I looked up to ConvertToStreamPass (where we put affinities on ops) and then scanned to see where ops stopped having `on(#hal.device.affinity...)` and then looked around. the first one I see is:

that then feeds into the first dispatch that has no affinity:
```mlir
stream.tensor.dispatch @extern_dispatch_1::@rocm_hsaco_fb::@f4gemm_kernel_func
```

this is likely caused by not having an annotation on that input. I don't see a flow.tensor.transfer on it. it looks like a silly fill -> pad, and since the fill does not have any placed origin/relation back to inputs it has no placement.

there may be ergonomics/etc improvements that could happen here - there may be interplay with hoisting, default affinities, etc - but the root cause is that there's no transfer there so we don't know precisely where to place it and today if you want good outputs you need to make sure we precisely place things.

The fix can be transferring the global load to the proper device. I manually add two lines and update the uses, and it works.

```mlir

    %hoisted_device1 = flow.tensor.transfer %__hoisted_tensor_f16 : tensor<f16> to #hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>

### What happened?

Compiling a subset of an fp4 quantized model with an assembly kernel appears to cause IREE incorrectly place certain executions on the wrong device (device 0 instead of device 1) and to break up execution into multiple smaller command buffers.

I have included mlirs and the resulting decode function traces. `same_device` and `same_device_2` are for two trimmed down transformer blocks that occur on the same device (blocks 61&62 on device 0 for `same_device` and blocks 63&64 for device 1 for `same_device_2`). `diff_device` also contains 2 blocks but on different devices: block 62 on device 0 and block 63 on device 1.

Both `same_device` and `same_device_2` contain a single command buffer on their respective devices (ignore the small execution on deivce 0 for `same_device_2`, it's the token embedding and needed to be included`). `diff_device` meanwhile has multiple command buffers on *both* devices as well as incorrectly mixing executions on devices 0 and 1 (at t=2.522s there is a command buffer with an f4gemm on deivce 0 that breaks up the execution on device 1).

and 

```

The first one has the operand `%72` which is on `device_0`. So that instance of the dispatch invocation (`%73) is supposed to be on device 0. The second one has the operand `%156` which is on device 1, and this instance of the dispatch (%156) is supposed to be on device 1.

    %hoisted_device0 = flow.tensor.transfer %__hoisted_tensor_f16 : tensor<f16> to #hal.device.affinity<@__device_0>

The first instance has one operand with affinity to device zero, and the second operand is from a global with default affinity. It should get affinity device 0
The second instance has one operand with affinity to device one, and the second operand is from a global with default affinity. It should get affinity device 1

that's what we'd need topology information for - we can't assume that a global instantiated in device 0's memory is accessible by device 1 (and the user may not want that). it's a cost model thing. big issue we need to fix, but via a bunch of knobs and stuff. the topology would let us at least get things in the right place, but it won't be efficient (unless unified and uniform memory access is available between the devices).

Okay, I'll leave it to @benvanik since we have a workaround. @Alex-Vasile I think you can disable hoisting (`--iree-opt-const-expr-hoisting=false`) for now.

```mlir
  util.global private @__hoisted_tensor_f16 {stream.affinity.default = #hal.device.affinity<@__device_0>} : tensor<f16>

Not sure if that's caused by export tools or what but the old "garbage-in garbage-out" saying comes to mind :)

(the parameter encoding stuff will make that less bad at least, because we bake them all out and store them in giant slabs - would still be nice not to have in programs not using that workflow, though)

I'd be fine adding an experimental flag to do something, but today we just produce inefficient programs and if we tried to quick fix this we'd produce programs that don't run or have incorrect results.

actually, the easiest fix would be to use topology information, but I forget how that's provided - it may not be too bad but I'd have to dig deeper. it may require the user provide a command line flag to set the topology, but that seems fine.

Is it because it is not performant? It is an option if we are looking for functioning and correctness.

I don't know anything unless I dig deeper.

Ok, that makes sense. 

One WAR might be to look through globals that are zero initialized and used on multiple devices and clone them? I know the issues that it might have, but if under a flag maybe that works. I am just throwing out ideas to see a way other than "disable hoisting"

Seems reasonable enough!

issue.body:
Replicates `IREE::Util::GlobalOps` that are used on multiple affinities and rewires their uses to the associated global. This will allow for specialization of globals for each affinity instead of having unspecialized and a copy each use.

The pass is added right before stream conversion; it is guarded under an experimental flag. The proper implementation is using topology information.

It is a workaround for https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/22081

### What happened?

I am seeing numerical differences between a trimmed down model when operating across 2 devices. I've tracked it down to the interaction of the following ops:
```python
	q = self.attn_q(x)
	k = self.attn_k(x)
	v = self.attn_v(x)
```
Which will performs a matmul on each using an asembly kernel.

Having all three matmuls performed produces numerical differences in the final result between pipeline parallelism of 2 and an unpipelined model. 

If **any** 1 of the `self.attn_q` calls is replaced with one of the following
```python
	q = x[..., : self.head_count * self.head_dim]
	k = x[..., : self.head_count_kv * self.head_dim]
	v = x[..., : self.head_count_kv * self.head_dim]
```
The results remain different between PP2 and unpipelined.

If however **any** 2 of the 3 are replaced, then the results become identical

I'm attaching all 7 permutations of the input mlirs. `_pp` indicates the pipelined version `_qkv` indicates that all three `q`, `k`, `v` values are calculated using the `self.attn_` calls; `_qk` indicates that only `q` and `k` are calculated using them, etc.

issue.body:
Extends the existing pass to replicate globals per affinity with a second mode: Instead of replicating globals, which is beneficial for performance, but increases the memory footprint, this new mode transfers the globals to each affinity where they are needed. Other passes could eliminate the transfers/copies where possible.

Similar to the replication, this is currently guarded by an experimental flag.

Fixes #22564.

issue.title: [Flow] Transfer globals per affinity instead of replicating

timeline.body:
A note about how I verify if it fixes the issue or not:

- Download the MLIR file from the [original issue](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/22081): https://gist.githubusercontent.com/MaheshRavishankar/6045e9ac1d921c55785eb7c5639c80ea/raw/27022b77962078f0ef5677693413d414a474f59d/llama_8b_fp16.mlir
- Compile the program to Stream.

```bash
iree-compile ~/llama_8b_fp16.mlir -o ~/fixed.stream.mlir \
    --compile-to=stream \
    --iree-hip-target=gfx950 \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[0]" \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[1]" \
    --iree-opt-level=O3 \
    --iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-collapse-across-expands=true \
    --iree-stream-affinity-solver-max-iterations=1024 \
    --iree-hal-indirect-command-buffers=true \
    --iree-stream-resource-memory-model=discrete \
    --iree-hip-specialize-dispatches \
    --iree-hal-memoization=true \
    --iree-codegen-enable-default-tuning-specs=true --iree-stream-experimental-replicate-globals-per-affinity
```

Track the SSA uses of `%arg4` in `@prefill_bs4$async`. With the flag, you should not see the copy ops within `stream.cmd.execute. E.g.,

```mlir
%13 = stream.tensor.import on(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>) %arg4 : !hal.buffer_view -> tensor<?x1048576xf8E4M3FN>{%11} in !stream.resource<external>{%12}

%297 = stream.cmd.execute on(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>) await(%198) => ... %13 as %arg12
// no copy on %arg12
```

Without the pass, we are seeing the copy.

```mlir
%13 = stream.tensor.import on(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>) %arg4 : !hal.buffer_view -> tensor<?x1048576xf8E4M3FN>{%11} in !stream.resource<external>{%12}
%42 = stream.tensor.import on(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>) %arg4 : !hal.buffer_view -> tensor<?x1048576xf8E4M3FN>{%17} in !stream.resource<external>{%31}

%313 = stream.cmd.execute ... %13 as %arg10
  stream.cmd.copy %arg10[%c0], %arg12[%70], %12 : !stream.resource<external>{%12} -> !stream.resource<transient>{%71}
```

issue.body:
The experimental pass to replicate globals per unique device affinity lived in Stream so far, but operates on Flow dialect before conversion to Stream.

Move the pass to Flow and place it right after executable cleanup in the flow pipeline if enabled through the experimental flag.
